message.content:
Yes—you can file a noise‑complaint in Atlanta, but the “local council” that handles it isn’t a separate municipal body; it’s handled through the City of Atlanta’s police department and the city’s online portal.

### How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta

| Step | What to Do | Where / How |
|------|------------|-------------|
| **1** | Gather details | Note the address, time, duration, and description of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs). |
| **2** | Call the non‑emergency police line | Dial **404‑656‑4000** (Atlanta Police Department) and let the dispatcher know you’re filing a noise complaint. |
| **3** | Use the online portal | Visit the City of Atlanta’s official website: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/> → “Services” → “Report a Problem” → “Noise Complaint.” Fill out the form with the same details you’d give over the phone. |
| **4** | Submit the form | After submitting, you’ll receive a confirmation number. Keep it for follow‑up. |
| **5** | Follow up | If the issue persists, call the police again or use the portal’s “Track a Complaint” feature (if available). |

### Contact Information

| Agency | Phone | Website |
|--------|-------|---------|
| Atlanta Police Department (Non‑Emergency) | **404‑656‑4000** | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/> |
| City of Atlanta Online Portal | – | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/> |

> **Tip:** If the noise is a recurring problem (e.g., a neighbor’s loud party), you can also file a formal complaint with the city’s Code Enforcement division, which handles repeated violations. Their contact is usually listed on the same “Report a Problem” page.

So, while there isn’t a separate “council” office for noise complaints, you can definitely report them through the city’s police department or online portal.
